coverage.assessment: The brandy, Albert's call, the coal lift, the lock and the balcony all hold. Two closing premises of the 'no one could have got in' logic were cut: 'no other possible hiding-place' and Julius's front-door reasoning. Julius's time at the safe was also cut, which weakens the setup for 028.

The tea scene no longer has Sir James and Julius accompany Tuppence. They speak at the bedroom door without being brought there. Julius's exit and return remain inferable. The boudoir and balcony geometry is intact.
Speaker tags added in the revision ('said Julius', 'said Sir James') are accurate. Turn-taking in the dictaphone, Bournemouth and Hall exchanges is coherent despite the trims.
'Evidently died in her sleep', 'possibly an overdose' and 'some hours' are preserved. No suspect is shown handling the chloral bottle.
Nothing premature is revealed. Two cuts lose source ambiguity: Tuppence's 'dreamt it' doubt and the narrator's retrospective-irony line about Sir James's 'simple words'.
The discovery's delayed-recognition rhythm is collapsed. Tuppence's dawn exuberance, her uneasy 'Yes', and her 'dream of Mr. Brown' line are trimmed. The core dialogue voices survive.
Both suspects remain plausible. Sir James's 'If it is luck' and Julius's withheld 'Nothing' still balance each other.
All five dependencies survive at both endpoints. Dependency 1 is slightly weakened locally by the cut of 'some time over the task' (see F6).

strengths: The brandy sequence keeps every planned step: washstand, redirection to the tantalus, Julius handing to Sir James, Sir James forcing it, Tuppence holding the glass.
Rita's broken 'Don't--leave----' / 'sleepy' / 'Mr.--Brown----' is preserved with its dashes and breath-level staging.
The chapter ends on the verbatim chloral and empty-bottle hook, with Tuppence's own memory of the upset glass motivating it.
The Bournemouth assumed-name reasoning and Sir James's 'curious--really very curious' reaction to Hall remain intact, so the next chapter has its setup.
summary: The revision keeps every planned clue intact: the brandy chain, Rita's whisper, the locked door and key, Hall at the Métropole, the photograph vow, Tuppence's intuition, 'If it is luck', the pause before 'Nothing', and the empty-bottle hook. Suspicion stays neutral. The revision's own extra cuts, beyond the first draft, cause several small losses. The locked-room premises are thinner. The two men are never brought to the bedroom door before they speak there. The discovery beat is rushed. Tuppence's ironic 'tone of those simple words' observation and Julius's lingering at the safe are gone. None of these blocks comprehension, and each can be repaired by restoring wording the first draft already had.
